items.title: US and China extend their tariff truce
items.summary: The US kept its suspension of higher “reciprocal” tariffs on Chinese goods, leaving the rate at 10%, and excluded some products from other China tariffs. China in turn agreed to drop retaliatory measures and lift sanctions on shipping firms.

items.title: US waives new Russia sanctions and tariffs
items.summary: President Trump waived the trade measures in a new Russia sanctions law days before they took effect, including duties on Russian goods and penalties for buying Russian oil and gas, after a separate diesel deal with Moscow.

items.title: Canada and EU launch “Alliance for the Future”
items.summary: Canada and the EU announced more than 20 measures, including talks on a digital trade agreement and European Investment Bank funding for Canadian critical-minerals projects.

items.title: EU–Mercosur free trade agreement
items.where: EU – Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay
items.summary: Signed in January after 25 years of talks, the deal covers about 700 million people and removes tariffs on more than 90% of trade between the blocs. It is expected to take effect by the end of 2026, pending ratification.

items.title: EU–Australia free trade agreement
items.summary: After eight years of talks, the EU and Australia signed a deal removing tariffs on almost all European goods and nearly all Australian critical-mineral exports, alongside a security and defence pact.

items.title: US takes control of some Venezuelan oil reserves
items.summary: In August President Trump announced a deal giving the US control of some Venezuelan oil reserves; in November the two governments added a military cooperation agreement.

items.title: Iran war, US blockade and energy prices
items.summary: The US is enforcing a naval blockade of Iran, and attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz continue. The war has driven up fuel prices worldwide, a major issue for voters in several countries.
